case2.answer: The Board of a scheduled commercial bank must approve policies and risk‑governance for all bank activities and, with RBI’s guidelines, may offer Doorstep Banking facilities. It must maintain regular off‑site and on‑site monitoring of banking outlets to ensure supervision, uninterrupted service and timely grievance redressal, and it must review outlet transactions to confirm that financial‑inclusion targets in unbanked rural areas are being met. The Board sets internal financial‑inclusion targets, captures centre‑wise and tier‑wise data on accounts, deposits, advances, remittances and balances, reviews this progress at least quarterly and provides the data to RBI when required. For NBFCs, the credit facility for financing an IPO subscription is capped at ₹1 crore per borrower.

citations.text: The Board shall ensure regular off-site and on-site monitoring system of the ‘Banking Outlet’ to ensure proper supervision, ‘uninterrupted service’ and timely addressing of customer grievances.
citations.best_sentence: and timely addressing of customer grievances.
citations.evidence_sentence: (1) Banking Outlets (i) The Board shall ensure regular off-site and on-site monitoring system of the ‘Banking Outlet’ to ensure proper supervision, ‘uninterrupted service’ and timely addressing of customer grievances. (ii) The Board shall regularly review and monitor the transactions in the Banking Outlets to see that banking services are being transacted in these outlets and more specifically the target customers for financial inclusion are getting the banking facilities in unbanked rural centres. (iii) The Board shall set internal targets for financial inclusion. Data on centrewise and tier-wise customer accounts and transactions (Type and number of accounts, deposits received, advances made, remittances processed, outstanding balances, etc.) should be captured on regular basis and the Board shall review the progress in this regard regularly, say on quarterly basis. (iv) The Board shall make the above data available to RBI as and when required and called for.

case3.answer: Digital lending arrangements are governed by the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025, and any co‑lending involving REs must also follow those Directions. A bank must provide a Key Fact Statement (KFS) and determine penal charges in accordance with the RBI (Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025. An NBFC must provide a KFS and determine penal charges as per the RBI (Non‑Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025.

Digital lending arrangements shall continue to be governed by Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time. Provided that, any digital lending arrangement involving co-lending by the REs shall, without derogation to Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025, be guided by the provisions of these Directions.
